adds.title: Executive Order 14168 ("Defending Women from Gender Ideology Extremism and Restoring Biological Truth to the Federal Government") - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Executive Order 14168 (signed 20 January 2025) directs US federal agencies, including the Bureau of Prisons, to recognize only two sexes, and federal practice has followed by placing transgender inmates in facilities congruent with their sex assigned at birth rather than their asserted gender identity. The ACLU said it had received reports that transgender women were being transferred to men's prisons, told they would be, or moved to solitary confinement, and the Bureau of Prisons stopped reporting the number of transgender people it holds. Advocates say the order violates the Prison Rape Elimination Act's requirement that trans inmates' housing be decided on an individual safety assessment. Federal custody rules apply in Puerto Rico as a US territory; the search found no separate Puerto Rico Department of Corrections trans-inmate housing policy, special unit, or ruling.

records.note: Only a US-federal-level placement rule could be sourced: Executive Order 14168 (Jan 2025) moved federal custody, which operates in Puerto Rico, to birth-sex placement for transgender inmates, with reports of transfers to men's facilities and solitary confinement and cessation of official trans-inmate counts. No territorial documentation was found for Puerto Rico's own Department of Corrections facilities on trans-inmate placement, special units, or segregation practice, and no Puerto Rico-specific case or ruling on trans prisoner housing surfaced in the searches and fetches performed.
